name: Notion
summary: Create a public connection in the Notion Developer portal and start OAuth right away, with no review. Only the optional Marketplace listing goes through a Notion review.

needs.label: Get listed on the Notion Marketplace

paths.label: Public connection
paths.detail: Any Notion user can connect your app.

paths.label: Listed on the Marketplace
paths.detail: You also want a public listing.

links.label: Create a connection
links.note: opens after Notion sign-in; Notion now calls integrations connections

links.label: Manage your connections
links.note: same developer portal; opens after Notion sign-in

links.label: Submit for Marketplace review
links.note: opens after Notion sign-in; go to Listings, then Connections; public connections set to Any workspace only

verdicts.why: You can start the OAuth flow as soon as the connection has client credentials and a redirect URI, with no Marketplace review.
A Marketplace listing goes through a Notion security review, and Notion says to expect a reply in 5 to 10 business days.

skip.note: Composio offers managed OAuth for Notion. Notion's hosted MCP server also supports dynamic client registration at mcp.notion.com/register, so an MCP client can connect with no app of your own.
whyOwnApp: You want your own connection name and capabilities shown on Notion's consent prompt.
You want a Marketplace listing, which needs your own public connection.
You want to set exactly which capabilities your app asks for.

requirements.label: A Notion account and development workspace
requirements.detail: You pick a development workspace when you create the connection in the Developer portal.

requirements.label: Redirect URI
requirements.detail: Where Notion sends users after they allow access, with a temporary code.

requirements.label: Installation scope set to Any workspace
requirements.detail: Pick Any workspace so anyone can install it. You cannot change this after creation.

requirements.label: A list of capabilities
requirements.detail: Pick the least you need. Fewer capabilities make it more likely a workspace admin can install your connection.

requirements.label: Marketplace listing details
requirements.detail: Listing name, description, category, tags, images and logo.

steps.title: Pick the right credential
steps.detail: Use a public connection when each user authorizes your app. A personal access token or internal connection only fits your own scripts or one workspace.

steps.title: Create the connection
steps.detail: In the Developer portal open Build, Connections, Create new connection. Enter the name, development workspace, redirect URIs, Any workspace and your capabilities.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab and store the OAuth client ID and secret. The authorization URL is also shown there.

steps.title: Write the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Send users to the authorization URL with owner=user. Exchange the code at api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Store tokens and refresh them
steps.detail: Save the access token, refresh token and bot_id. A refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token.

steps.title: Test with your own workspace
steps.detail: Run the flow yourself and pick some pages in the page picker. Your app only sees the pages you pick.

steps.title: Draft and submit the listing
steps.detail: Start a new connection listing under Listings, Connections, fill in the details and submit it for review.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's review
steps.detail: The Notion team reviews every listing and replies by email. If changes are needed, fix them and resubmit.

scopes.name: Read content
scopes.meaning: Read existing pages, databases and blocks.

scopes.name: Update content
scopes.meaning: Change existing pages and blocks, but not create new ones.

scopes.name: Insert content
scopes.meaning: Create new pages and blocks. It does not grant reading full objects.

scopes.name: Read comments
scopes.meaning: List comments on a page or block.

scopes.name: Insert comments
scopes.meaning: Add comments to a page or an existing discussion.

scopes.name: User information with email addresses
scopes.meaning: User objects include name, profile image and email.

limits.title: 3 requests per second per connection
limits.detail: 180 requests per minute on most plans, 600 per minute on Business and Enterprise. Data source queries have a separate limit of about 3 per second.

limits.title: 1000 blocks or 500KB per request
limits.detail: Payloads max out at 1000 block elements and 500KB. Block and rich text arrays are capped at 100 items.

limits.title: Installation scope is permanent
limits.detail: Only Any workspace connections can be listed on the Marketplace. If you picked selected workspaces, you must create a new connection.

limits.title: Every user authorizes separately
limits.detail: Only the user who authorized can use the connection in their workspace. Teammates each run the flow themselves.

limits.title: Access is limited to picked pages
limits.detail: Users choose pages in the page picker, and sharing a parent page shares its children. Users can change access later.

blockers.symptom: API calls fail on a page the user can see in Notion.
blockers.fix: The page was not shared with your connection. Ask the user to re-run the flow and pick it, or add your connection from the page's Add connections menu.
Wait for the Retry-After header, then back off with jitter. Queue requests so one job does not use the whole budget.

blockers.symptom: A user on an Enterprise workspace cannot install your connection.
blockers.fix: Enterprise owners can restrict connections to an approved list. Ask the owner to approve it, and request fewer capabilities.

blockers.symptom: Existing users are asked to connect again.
blockers.fix: You changed capabilities, so users must re-authenticate. Settle capabilities before launch.

blockers.symptom: Your connection is not eligible for a Marketplace listing.
blockers.fix: It was created with selected workspaces. Create a new connection with Any workspace.

sources.title: Capabilities
sources.note: Notion uses capabilities set in the portal, not OAuth scope strings. None of them trigger a review.

sources.title: Notion MCP authorization server metadata
sources.note: Returned registration_endpoint https://mcp.notion.com/register, S256 PKCE, token auth method none allowed, and client_id_metadata_document_supported true.

sources.title: Composio Notion toolkit
sources.note: Says Composio-managed OAuth available: Yes. Auth schemes OAuth 2.0 and API key.

unverified: Notion docs do not say how long access tokens last before you must refresh.
Notion's OAuth docs for the REST API do not mention PKCE support.
The docs say creating an internal connection needs a workspace owner, but do not say the same for public connections.
